title: EU accession as an instrument for speeding up transition
summary_en: Halpern reviews how EU accession functioned as a transition-acceleration instrument for the Central-Eastern European member states, drawing on the Hungarian experience as the running example. The chapter argues that the accession conditionality bundle (acquis adoption, single-market access, structural funds) compressed reform timelines that would otherwise have taken decades, but also created new dependencies on EU policy frameworks and FDI inflows. [Book-chapter survey; abstract not publicly available — title-based summary, verification recommended.]
data_used: Hungarian and CEE macroeconomic series (output, FDI, trade openness) and qualitative review of EU accession-conditionality milestones. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Useful background reading for Hungarian EU-policy strategy (KKM, NGM EU Funds department): frames why EU membership has been net-positive for Hungary on growth and reform speed, and identifies the dependencies (FDI reliance, EU-fund concentration in selected sectors) that current Hungarian policy debates over the 'New Era' agenda are trying to renegotiate.
